verdict.reasoning: Patient states anxiety has been present for "about two months or so" coinciding with starting a new job: "I would say maybe about two months or so, I've been feeling like this".
Patient describes palpitations: "I find my, my heart kind of racing" and "just a constant like, rapid heart beating".
Patient reports difficulty sleeping: goes to bed at 10–11 pm, "Not for ages, I'm, I'm lying awake all night" and estimates only "maybe, three, four hours" of shallow sleep.
Patient says, "I work for a, a, a fashion retailer, in um, the head office team," and that this is a new job: "me starting a new job".
Patient describes boss and work stress: "my boss is not very nice to me" and "it's been really stressful I think over the past two months".

Patient feels dread but still attends work: "I just really dread, going there" and later, "No, 'cause I think that would just add to the tension, but I do like pretty much every morning I think, ohh I should call in sick or like, just not go."
Sleep onset: Doctor asks, "what time do you go to bed" and patient replies "About ten, eleven" and then says "Not for ages, I'm, I'm lying awake all night," indicating prolonged sleep onset latency.

Patient mentions waking before alarm with racing heart: "I find myself waking up before that, 'cause I'm just my heart is racing" and shallow short sleep: "even when I'm in sleep it's such a shallow sleep, but maybe, three, four hours, I'm getting now."

While morning palpitations, irregular feeling, and duration are supported ("when I realise in the morning that... I feel like I'm gonna be late"; "Irregular, I think"; "couple of minutes... like ten minutes"), the claim of occurring "without chest pain" conflicts with transcript: patient answers chest pain question with, "No, um, well yeah it's painful to , when the heart, when my heart is beating fast".

Daytime fatigue and anhedonia: "It's just, really, really low... I find no enjoyment at all" and "anything that, previously was, really fun is just not, it's not enjoyable." Decreased socializing/exercise: "I know that I'm not gonna have fun, because I don't want to, go out" and "I did used to like to like go running, and... play tennis... but now... I'm not going out to do that quite so much." Feeling on edge: "I'm like, yeah, on edge the whole time."
Public transport anxiety: "I find public transport really stressful anyway, especially being on the tube it's, 'cause it's quite, getting warmer so it's just really airless."

Persistently low mood: "I'm pretty much, down... even at the weekends and stuff it's just the, kind of like constant, feeling of just being a bit, down, a bit unhappy." Denies suicidal thoughts: "I haven't had any suicidal thoughts or any, thoughts that have been that extreme" and no suggestion of homicidal ideation anywhere.
Patient states, "I have a good support system, like I do have good family and stuff."

Appetite: patient says, "Probably, not, significant changes maybe. No I wouldn't say that, I wouldn't say that I'm eating like, much differently. Ohh that, I probably have more chocolate than normal" and confirms regular eating: Doctor: "You're eating regularly otherwise?" Patient: "Yeah".
Living situation: "Yeah, I live with my parents, just my parents."

Smoking and alcohol: "I try not to smoke, but I do, occasionally"; for alcohol, patient reports "probably quite a lot on the Friday or Saturday... I probably go over my limit just on those days, anyway, and then like, maybe a glass of wine during the week."
Illicit drugs: "I try not to smoke, but I do, occasionally, but I don't take drugs."
Family history: "I talk to my mum, because she also suffers from, well she's , suffered from like depression in the past."

Work-related anxiety: symptoms mainly around work stress and dread of going to work; insomnia and low mood described; patient clearly denies suicidal ideation: "I haven't had any suicidal thoughts" and there is no mention of homicidal ideation.

Doctor assessment: "in terms of palpitations, it is most likely to be a, , associated with anxiety" and onset linked to same timeframe as anxiety: patient says palpitations only "in the past... couple of months".
Doctor advises self-referral: "you can self-refer via the NHS, for what we call like, talking therapy..." and "So I can send you the link for that." (i.e., CBT-type therapy).
Online resources: "There are some online resources that are really helpful. Um, can put the details, on there and you can, get on with them straight away and try and work through them as well."
Sleep hygiene: "And I'll put some more information on your notes about, helping with your, sleep patterns and things like that."

Safety-net: "if you're feeling like it's not helping at all, or your anxiety is getting worse, to the point where you can't cope with work, or you can't, just do your normal things day-to-day. Then, it's important for us to, for you to give us a call, back and just discuss that, further."
Medications as non–first-line: "some people, with anxiety they, do need to take medication to control that but that's, not something that we'd suggest in the first instance."
Blood tests and booking: "it's probably worth having couple of basic blood tests" and "So if you call the support line you can arrange the, to have the blood test done."
Follow-up: "then arranging a GP follow-up a week after you've had the tests, so we can just go through the results with you" and doctor says palpitations are "most likely... associated with anxiety."
